title: Anyone can send a question from a gym's web page in another person's name and mobile number
what: The 'Ask the gym' form on a gym's web page takes a typed name and a typed mobile number and never checks that the number belongs to the sender (the Join online form does check, with WhatsApp). The question lands in the gym's Enquiries under that number, and if that number already has an open enquiry the new question and name are added to the real person's enquiry. The gym then calls or messages a person who never asked anything. The form can also be sent straight to the gym server, skipping the 5-a-day limit per network address, and 40 questions in a day from anyone close the form for every real visitor of that gym until the next day.
expected: A web page question is kept only after the sender proves the number (the same WhatsApp check Join online uses), or it is marked 'number not checked' and never added to someone's existing enquiry; the gym's daily limit cannot be used up by one sender.
who: gym owners and any person whose number is typed in
how_often: whenever someone types a number that is not theirs
fix_line: Ask for the WhatsApp number check before a web page question is kept, or keep unchecked questions apart and never merge them into an existing enquiry

title: Anyone with the public app key can list every gym's web page photos, unpublished drafts included
what: The photo store's read rule lets a file be read while it is on a gym's page row, published or not. The store's 'list' call uses the same rule, so anyone holding the public app key (it is inside every app) can list the photos of every gym that has a page, including pages the owner has not published yet, and each file's folder name is that gym's internal id. The file itself notes this as a known limit.
expected: Photos of a page that is not published can be seen only by that gym's own people; the public can list nothing and can open only photos of published pages.
who: gym owners preparing a web page
how_often: any time, by anyone who tries
fix_line: Let the public read only photos of published pages, and show unpublished drafts to the owner through a signed link

title: Reads of gym data made with the server's master app key are never recorded
what: The new direct-read record writes down every look at gym data made with the database owner login, and owners are told every look is recorded. Looks made with the server's master app key (the key the HQ and panel Workers use, which anyone with the Supabase dashboard can copy) are left out on purpose, so a person who copies that key can read every gym's members and money through the normal web address with no record at all.
expected: Every look at a gym's data that is not the app itself serving that gym is recorded, including looks made with the master app key outside the Workers; or that key is kept where no person can copy it and the promise says so.
how_often: only if a person reads data with the master app key
fix_line: Record reads made with the master app key that do not come from the Workers (for example by giving the Workers their own key), or change the promise to say what is not recorded

title: No test proves another gym cannot cancel this gym's personal-training booking, edit its trainer page, or turn off its browser alerts
what: The code limits each of these to the caller's own gym, but the database tests try another gym only for the week schedule and for booking with this gym's trainer. Nobody tests another gym's key cancelling a booking by its id, saving a trainer page for this gym's trainer, or removing this gym's saved browser for alerts. A later change could open them and every test would still pass.
expected: Each call that takes a booking, a person or a browser address has a test where another gym's key is refused and the row is unchanged.
how_often: only if a later change breaks the gym check
fix_line: Add three refusals with the other gym's key to the trainer schedule and browser alert tests

items.reason: All 194 functions listed for 0063-0098 mapped against the catalog. Every underscore helper and every hq_* call (MettleUp billing and checks, QA gym purge, AI wallet grant, paid alerts, browser push, digests, web page switch, read record) is service_role only: the advisor lists none of them as runnable by visitors or signed-in users, which also covers default PUBLIC rights. Open to any visitor (anon and authenticated): owner_* calls take the gym only from the key and every row id they take is matched to that gym (receipt, booking, trainer, thread, AI task, alert, person); member_* calls take the gym from the member key; phone_sign_in_find, member_find_gyms and self_join_send need a WhatsApp proof; ai_question_take, ai_visitor_question_take and self_join_pay_gym need the panel Worker's signature; ai_question_back is unsigned but needs a random question id only the Worker holds. gym_page_ask_send takes a typed number with no proof (new finding 01). 0091's new helpers, 0092 and 0094 are not on the live server (no grants in the catalog). 0097 and 0098 say NOT APPLIED in their first line, but their tables and calls are in the live catalog, so those headers are stale.

Tables reached only through the key with no gym or row id to point elsewhere (gym_alert_settings, gym_ai_member_rules, gym_ai_questions, gym_ai_question_slots) cannot be pointed at another gym. Server-only tables (no per-gym rule; checked that apps cannot read them): gym_plan_changes, gym_checkouts, receipt_counters, gym_billing_reminders, member_find_tries, gym_page_reports, gym_page_asks, db_read_log_state. Gaps: see L3.3.

Rule applied. Every per-gym table has some second-gym test, but three calls that take a row id have none: cancelling a personal-training booking, saving a trainer page, and removing a saved browser for alerts. One new finding.
Rule applied: no live cross-gym attempt was run; only code, tests and the catalog file were read.

All 41 key pattern hits in these files are the role name service_role in grant lines or comments, not keys. The web push signing key (VAPID) is only named, never written here. But reads made with the master app key are never recorded by the new read record: new finding 03.

No AI key lives in these files. AI spending is guarded on the server: every AI question needs the panel Worker's signature with a 5-minute clock, a gym spends only its own credits, with daily limits per member (10), visitor (3), staff (60) and per gym (200 members, 30 visitors), and a monthly member limit the owner sets. The give-back call is unsigned but needs a random id. Owner AI spend and refund are owner-only.

No PIN or password call lives here. Phone sign-in and Find my gym need a WhatsApp proof and allow at most 5 searches per proof; a bad proof answers BAD_PROOF only. Messages have per-member limits. Owner and staff keys used by every owner_* call here still never expire (existing finding reused); browser alerts stop when the sign-in that saved them ends.

No query is built from typed text: the only dynamic SQL in these files rebuilds fixed constraints or role settings with quoted names. Typed text is length-capped and trimmed (messages 1000, page about 500, questions 500); web addresses are refused in page text and questions; the photo address and Maps link are matched to fixed patterns. The public page HTML is escaped by the panel Worker.

Two uploads here. Trainer photo: a JPEG in text form, at most about 100 KB, checked by its first bytes, owner or that trainer only. Web page photos: owner-only slot, one fixed file name per slot, WebP only, 1 MB, no overwrite, 12 open and 60 a day per gym. Faults: the read rule lets anyone list every gym's page photos including unpublished drafts (new finding 02); files of removed photos are never deleted and a 'Start demo' owner key can also take slots, the same no-clean-up fault as the existing demo photo hosting finding.

Gym web pages live at a chosen name and are public by design, only when published, not hidden by HQ, not switched off, gym not suspended. A published page shows the gym's join code, and the join-online preview answers any code with no try limit, so the existing guessable join code finding covers both. Photo names are 32 random letters. The ask and report forms share one daily limit per gym that one sender can use up (existing shared-cap finding), and Ask takes an unproven number (new finding 01).

These database files pull in no package; the only extension they turn on (pgaudit) is the one Supabase ships and updates. The CVE list's manifests are the app package lock and two Android build files, none in this area.
